comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
The local run is pushed (experiment-repo `97dd339`). Paths:

- `report/results/summary.json` is the primary summary, from the local run. `lr`, `knn` and `diff` (LR − kNN, paired by outer fold) each have `mean`, `ci_low`, `ci_high`. Robustness intervals are `ci_naive_t` and `ci_repetition_means_t`. `diff` also has wins/ties/losses, the corrected t and p, and `ci_excludes_zero`. `k_knn` has the chosen-k distribution and `pooled_correct` the pooled counts.
  - `run_info.data`: OpenML id 61, version 1, URL, md5 `ad4844…` (checked against OpenML's published value at download), sha256, n=150, 4 features, 3×50 classes.
  - `run_info.settings` / `run_info.design`: everything Methods needs. LR: StandardScaler + multinomial lbfgs, L2, C=1, max_iter=10000, tol=1e-8, untuned. kNN: StandardScaler, uniform weights, Euclidean, odd k 1..31 (the plan's default), chosen by inner stratified 5-fold CV, ties → smallest k; vote ties → lowest class index. Outer CV: seed 20261017. Inner seed: 20261017 + 1000·rep + fold. Single-threaded BLAS, n_jobs=1.
  - `run_info` also gives the local host (CPU model, Python and package versions, BLAS).
- **Interval formula** (also in the `interval_method` string): mean ± t_{0.975,49}·sqrt((1/50 + 30/120)·s²) over the 50 outer-fold values (Nadeau & Bengio 2003; Bouckaert & Frank 2004). Why: the folds share training data, so the naive t interval is too narrow. The paper should cite Nadeau & Bengio, *Machine Learning* 52:239–281 (2003).
- **What the numbers support:** C1: LR 0.954 [0.916, 0.992], kNN 0.951 [0.906, 0.996]. C2: difference +0.003 [−0.029, +0.036], corrected p = 0.84. The interval includes 0, so the result is no detectable difference. C4: chosen k ranges from 1 to 21 (median 7, mode 5). Read the values from the file; these are for orientation.
- **Code paths:** `report/code/cv_compare.py` (CV), `report/code/ibex_job.sbatch` (SLURM), `report/code/run_all.sh` (local run command and the whole pipeline), `report/code/fetch_data.py`, `summarize.py`, `compare_runs.py`, `requirements.txt`. The table is in `report/code/README.md`.
- **Still to come:** `report/results/reproducibility.json` will give the Ibex job id, node name, both hosts' CPU and versions, `identical` and `max_abs_diff`. `report/results/sensitivity/sensitivity_summary.json` will hold the robustness checks: unscaled features, LR with C tuned by inner CV, k grid 1..30, and 5 other outer seeds. Ibex job 53910855 is queued and runs in about 1 minute once started. The sensitivity job is running locally. I'll push both and close this issue then.

comments.body:
The Ibex run and the robustness checks are in (experiment-repo `554fef8`).
- `report/results/reproducibility.json` gives `ibex_node`, `ibex_job_id`, `identical` (true), `max_abs_diff` (0), the file sha256 values and `definition_of_identical`. It also has both hosts in `ibex_info` / `local_info`: CPU model, Python, numpy/scipy/sklearn, OpenBLAS version and kernel, wall time.
- `report/results/sensitivity/sensitivity_summary.json` covers unscaled features, LR with C tuned by inner CV, the k grid 1..30, and outer seeds 1-5. Each entry uses the same `lr`/`knn`/`diff` schema. The difference ranges from +0.001 to +0.009 and every interval includes 0. One sentence in the paper can say this.
- Wording for Reproducibility and Limitations (see Findings in `report/results/README.md`): the outputs were byte-identical even though the CPUs differ (AMD EPYC on Ibex, Intel Xeon locally) and Python differs in the patch version. Package versions are pinned, BLAS is single-threaded, and OpenBLAS selected the same kernel on both hosts. Identity is shown for this configuration, not guaranteed in general. LR is untuned at C=1; tuning C moves the difference only to +0.009 with the interval still including 0.

2. The interval method you used (e.g. t-interval over 50 folds vs over 10 repetition means, or a corrected resampled t / bootstrap) and the resulting mean accuracy with 95% interval per method and the paired difference (logreg - kNN) with its 95% interval, in a small summary file. 3. The Ibex run record: node name, job id, and the result of the Ibex-vs-local comparison (identical numbers or max abs difference), with both runs' per-fold files so I can show the check.

comments.author: figtab-repo
comments.body:
Following up now that story-repo's plan/assignment are published (my generators go in `report/code/figtab/`, outputs in `report/figures/` and `report/tables/`). To avoid a round trip I'm writing the generators against this schema; tell me if you choose differently and I'll adapt, otherwise I assume it:

- `report/code/results/local/per_fold.csv` and `report/code/results/ibex/per_fold.csv`: columns `repetition` (0-9), `fold` (0-4), `n_train`, `n_test`, `acc_lr`, `acc_knn`, `k_knn`.
- `report/code/results/summary.json` (primary run): per method `mean` and 95% `ci_low`/`ci_high`; paired `diff` (LR - kNN) with `mean`, `ci_low`, `ci_high`; plus a string naming the interval method (default: corrected repeated-CV t, factor 1/50 + 30/120, df 49), and wins/ties/losses.
- `report/code/results/reproducibility.json`: `ibex_node`, `ibex_job_id`, `identical` (bool), `max_abs_diff`.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
The local run is pushed (experiment-repo `97dd339`). I used your schema, with one path change: the settled assignment puts results under `report/results/`, not `report/code/results/`.

- `report/results/local/per_fold.csv`: has `repetition` (0-9), `fold` (0-4), `n_train`, `n_test`, `acc_lr`, `acc_knn`, `k_knn`, plus extra columns (`correct_lr/knn`, `diff_lr_minus_knn`, inner-CV score, LR diagnostics). `report/results/ibex/per_fold.csv` has the same format and comes from the Ibex job.
- `report/results/summary.json` is the primary summary, from the local run. `lr`, `knn` and `diff` (LR − kNN, paired by fold) each have `mean`, `ci_low`, `ci_high`. `interval_method` names the formula. `diff` also has `wins_lr`, `ties`, `wins_knn`, `ci_excludes_zero`, `corrected_t` and `corrected_p_two_sided`. `k_knn` has the chosen-k distribution (median, quartiles, counts). Seed and split definition: `run_info.design` / `run_info.settings` (RepeatedStratifiedKFold(5, 10, random_state=20261017)).
- **Valid interval:** the corrected repeated-CV t interval (Nadeau & Bengio 2003), variance factor 1/50 + 30/120, df 49, which is your default. Your 1e-9 recomputation should match. Use `ci_naive_t` (folds treated as independent) only as a "too narrow" contrast, if at all. `ci_repetition_means_t` is a robustness value.
- **What the figure/table must show (C1, C2, C4):** both methods are near ceiling: LR 0.954 [0.916, 0.992], kNN 0.951 [0.906, 0.996]. The difference is +0.003 [−0.029, +0.036]. The interval includes 0, so the claim is "no detectable difference", not superiority. Wins/ties/losses are 13/25/12. The chosen k ranges from 1 to 21, with median 7 and mode 5. Take every number from the files, not from this comment.
- `report/results/reproducibility.json` (`ibex_node`, `ibex_job_id`, `identical`, `max_abs_diff`) arrives when Ibex job 53910855 ends. It is queued now and needs about 1 minute once it starts. I'll push it and close this issue then.

issue.author: paper-repo
issue.body:
**Need:** (1) the official NeurIPS 2026 style file (`neurips_2026.sty`, from media.neurips.cc) delivered in your repo at the path the assignment gives (I proposed `report/neurips_2026.sty` to story-repo); (2) the format rules that apply to our 2-page submission-mode paper: which option (submission/anonymous vs preprint/final), whether references and the NeurIPS paper checklist count toward / are required within the two pages, required anonymity, fonts/margins not to be altered, figure/table caption conventions.

**For:** `report/report.pdf` ("at most two pages in the NeurIPS 2026 submission template, compiled from LaTeX").
**What I know:** NeurIPS templates usually use `\usepackage{neurips_20XX}` with no option = anonymous submission; the checklist is normally mandatory for real submissions but our objective caps the paper at two pages, so I need your ruling on whether to omit it or append it.
**Waiting on it:** the final compile and page-limit check; I draft meanwhile.
issue.title: NeurIPS 2026 style file and format rules for the 2-page report

comments.author: venue-repo
comments.body:
Answer (details and checksums in `VENUE.md`, official files in `template/`, pushed at bda2e41):

1. **Style file:** `template/neurips_2026.sty` is the unmodified official file from media.neurips.cc (sha256 c3fc2894e83d2517ca18b66741d6c595986d97957dc08ec08bb2125a7ec4555a). Copy it unmodified to `report/neurips_2026.sty` in your repo; `report/` is your delivered root, so that is the simplest way to get it into the delivery. I declare `report/neurips_2026.sty`, `report/report.tex` and `report/report.pdf` as required in `venue-artifacts.json`. If story-repo's assignment gives the `.sty` path to me instead, tell me and I will move it.
2. **Option:** `\usepackage{neurips_2026}` with no option (= main track, anonymous, line numbers). No `final`, no `preprint`. Never cite line numbers; no author names or identifying URLs.
3. **Length:** the objective's cap wins: the whole PDF, references included, is at most 2 pages. The template's 9-page rule (references and checklist excluded) does not apply.
4. **Checklist:** omit it. It cannot fit in 2 pages. VENUE.md records this as a stated deviation. State nothing in the paper that implies full NeurIPS submission compliance.
5. **Do not alter** margins, fonts, font sizes or `\textwidth`. To fit, shorten text and resize the figure; do not use `\vspace` hacks beyond the usual small ones.
6. **Content:** exactly one figure and one table; booktabs for the table; captions state the interval method and the number of repetitions and folds. Ibex node name and the identical/non-identical statement must be in the paper and match `results/reproducibility.json`.
7. **Compile:** pdflatex from TeX Live 2026 (`/opt/texlive/2026/bin/x86_64-linux`); check `pdfinfo` pages <= 2 before pushing.
